description: Security Ops — CrowdSec engine, bouncer, and AppSec (WAF) observability. Metrics scraped from the CrowdSec security engine's Prometheus endpoint on :6060 (cs_* series). Many panels stay EMPTY until (a) the engine is scraped, (b) real traffic/attacks flow through Traefik, and (c) the CrowdSec Console / CAPI enrollment and AppSec engine are configured. NOTE on per-IP data: CrowdSec deliberately does NOT expose per-IP decisions in Prometheus (unbounded cardinality) — 'top blocked IPs' lives in `cscli decisions list` / the LAPI, not here.

panels.description: Currently-active decisions (bans/captchas) held by the LAPI, summed across all origins (crowdsec local scenarios, CAPI community blocklist, subscribed lists, manual cscli). Metric: cs_active_decisions (gauge; labels reason, origin, action). POPULATES once attacks are seen locally or the CrowdSec Console/CAPI is enrolled (community blocklist) — reads empty/0 until then, which is expected on a fresh engine.
panels.title: Active Decisions (bans)

panels.description: Locally-generated decisions in the last 24h, proxied by bucket overflows (each scenario overflow raises one alert → one decision). Metric: increase(cs_bucket_overflowed_total[24h]). NOTE: this counts only LOCAL scenario decisions — CAPI/list-sourced decisions bump the active-decisions gauge without a local overflow, so this undercounts total additions.
panels.title: Decisions Added (24h, local)

panels.description: Local alerts raised in the last 24h (bucket overflows). Metric: increase(cs_bucket_overflowed_total[24h]). Locally, alerts ≈ decisions added; this stays empty until a scenario actually overflows (needs malicious traffic).
panels.title: Alerts (24h)

panels.description: LAPI / engine reachability. Uses the CrowdSec LAPI pod's cs_info metric as the up signal: 1 = the LAPI is being scraped and serving. Metric: max(up{namespace="crowdsec",pod=~"crowdsec-lapi.*"}). The scrape job label is kubernetes-pods (Alloy), so components are distinguished by the pod-name prefix, not a crowdsec job.
panels.title: LAPI / Engine Up

panels.description: Number of CrowdSec agent (parser/bucket engine) pods reporting metrics — one cs_info series per agent pod. With the agent running as a DaemonSet this should equal the node count. Metric: count(cs_info{namespace="crowdsec",pod=~"crowdsec-agent.*"}).
panels.title: Agents Reporting

panels.description: Whether the AppSec (WAF) engine pod is up and scraped, via its cs_info metric. Metric: max(up{namespace="crowdsec",pod=~"crowdsec-appsec.*"}). NOTE: this reads 1 as soon as the appsec pod is running; the cs_appsec_* traffic series (reqs/blocks/rule hits) stay EMPTY until Traefik forwards requests to it (:7422) and rules match.
panels.title: AppSec Engines Up

panels.description: Rate of new bans over time, proxied by bucket overflows/s (local decisions being created). Metric: rate(cs_bucket_overflowed_total[$__rate_interval]). Total line = all scenarios; empty until scenarios overflow.
panels.title: Bans / Decisions Added Over Time (overflows/s)

panels.description: Active decisions broken down by origin: crowdsec (local scenarios), CAPI (community blocklist), lists (subscribed blocklists), cscli (manual). Metric: cs_active_decisions by origin. This is where CAPI/list enrollment shows up — expect the bulk of decisions from CAPI once Console-enrolled.
panels.title: Active Decisions by Origin

panels.description: Share of active decisions by scenario (the `reason` label on cs_active_decisions = the scenario that triggered the ban, e.g. crowdsecurity/http-probing). Empty until decisions exist.
panels.title: Active Decisions by Scenario

panels.description: Share of active decisions by origin (crowdsec / CAPI / lists / cscli). Metric: cs_active_decisions by origin.
panels.title: Active Decisions by Origin (share)

panels.description: Share of active decisions by action (ban, captcha, ...). Metric: cs_active_decisions by action.
panels.title: Decisions by Action

panels.description: Top scenarios by number of currently-active decisions (reason label). Effectively 'what is getting banned the most right now'. Metric: cs_active_decisions by reason.
panels.title: Top Scenarios (active decisions)

panels.description: Top scenarios by bucket overflows in the last 24h — which detection scenarios are firing most. Metric: increase(cs_bucket_overflowed_total[24h]) by name. Empty until scenarios overflow.
panels.title: Top Bucket Overflows (24h)

options.content: **Top blocked IPs is intentionally not shown here.** CrowdSec does **not** expose per-IP decisions in Prometheus (per-IP labels would be unbounded cardinality). The metrics only carry `reason` (scenario), `origin`, and `action`. For the actual banned-IP list use **`cscli decisions list`**, the CrowdSec Console, or query the LAPI `/v1/decisions` endpoint — not this dashboard.

panels.description: LIVE. Log lines read into the parsers per second, by acquisition source. Metric: rate(cs_parser_hits_total[$__rate_interval]) (labels source, type) on the agent pods. Total line = all sources.
panels.title: Lines Parsed/s (by acquisition source)

panels.description: LIVE. Parse failures per second — parser hits that did NOT match (a proxy for malformed/unrecognized log lines). Metric: rate(cs_parser_hits_ko_total[$__rate_interval]) by source. Sustained non-zero = a log format the parsers don't understand (check the acquisition config). Should sit near zero once acquisition matches the log sources.
panels.title: Parse Failures/s (unmatched)

panels.description: Buckets overflowing per second, by scenario — the core detection signal (an overflow = a scenario fired). Metric: rate(cs_bucket_overflowed_total[$__rate_interval]) by name.
panels.title: Buckets Overflowing (by scenario)

panels.description: Events poured into leaky buckets per second, by source — how much traffic each acquisition source is contributing to detection. Metric: rate(cs_bucket_poured_total[$__rate_interval]) (labels source, type, name).
panels.title: Events Poured to Buckets/s (by source)

panels.description: HTTP requests inspected by the AppSec engine per second, by source. Metric: rate(cs_appsec_reqs_total[$__rate_interval]) (labels source, appsec_engine). EMPTY until an AppSec engine is configured and Traefik forwards requests to it (:7422).
panels.title: AppSec Requests Inspected/s

panels.description: AppSec requests inspected per second, grouped by appsec_engine. Metric: rate(cs_appsec_reqs_total[$__rate_interval]) summed by appsec_engine. NOTE: this build exposes no cs_appsec_rule_hits / cs_appsec_block_total counters, so per-rule and blocked breakdowns aren't available — this is the only AppSec traffic signal on tap.
panels.title: AppSec Requests by Engine

panels.description: LAPI requests coming FROM the Traefik bouncer, per second, by bouncer. Metric: rate(cs_lapi_bouncer_requests_total[$__rate_interval]) (labels bouncer, route, method). POPULATES once a bouncer is bound to the LAPI — a healthy traefik bouncer polls /v1/decisions/stream on a fixed interval, so a flat non-zero rate = the bouncer is alive and talking to LAPI. Empty until then.
panels.title: LAPI Requests from Bouncer/s

panels.description: LAPI HTTP request rate by route (e.g. /v1/decisions/stream, /v1/heartbeat, /v1/watchers). Metric: rate(cs_lapi_route_requests_total{pod=~"crowdsec-lapi.*"}[$__rate_interval]) by route. NOTE: this build exposes no cs_lapi_decisions_ok_total/ko_total counters, so per-bouncer ok/ko lookup accounting isn't available — route-level request rate is the closest live signal of bouncer/agent polling.
panels.title: LAPI Requests/s by route

panels.description: Active decisions currently served to bouncers (the enforcement set the Traefik bouncer pulls). Same source as the overview KPI. Metric: sum(cs_active_decisions).
panels.title: Active Decisions Served

panels.description: Aggregate LAPI HTTP request rate across all routes (agent + bouncer polling). Metric: sum(rate(cs_lapi_route_requests_total{pod=~"crowdsec-lapi.*"}[$__rate_interval])). NOTE: this build exposes no cs_lapi_decisions_ko_total error counter, so this repurposes the route-request rate as a liveness/throughput signal — a steady non-zero value means the LAPI is being polled.
panels.title: LAPI Requests/s (total)

panels.description: Total CrowdSec component pods scraped (lapi + agent + appsec), via cs_info. >=1 = the security engine is scraped and serving. Metric: count(cs_info{namespace="crowdsec"}).
panels.title: Components Up

panels.description: CrowdSec version string, read from the cs_info metric's version label. Metric: cs_info{namespace="crowdsec"} (label version).
panels.title: Engine Version

panels.description: Time the Alloy scrape of the CrowdSec pods took. Metric: scrape_duration_seconds{namespace="crowdsec"} (scrape meta-series carry the target's namespace/pod labels; the job label is kubernetes-pods).
panels.title: Scrape Duration

panels.description: Series scraped from the CrowdSec pods — a rough proxy for engine metric richness. Metric: scrape_samples_scraped{namespace="crowdsec"}.
panels.title: Series Scraped

panels.description: Scrape duration over time per CrowdSec pod — watch for creep as decision/series count grows. Metric: scrape_duration_seconds{namespace="crowdsec"}.
panels.title: Scrape Duration Over Time

panels.description: LIVE. Whitelist hits per second by source — parser/scenario nodes that MATCHED a whitelist and were suppressed. Proves internal/trusted traffic is being whitelisted (not banned). Metric: rate(cs_node_wl_hits_ok_total[$__rate_interval]) by source (labels source, type, name) on the agent pods.
panels.title: Whitelist Hits/s (by source)

panels.description: LIVE. Average parse time per event, by parser type/source — how long the agent spends parsing each event. Metric: rate(cs_parsing_time_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval]) / rate(cs_parsing_time_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]) on the agent pods. Watch for creep under heavy log volume.
panels.title: Avg Parse Time/event

panels.description: LIVE. LAPI HTTP request rate by route (e.g. /v1/decisions/stream, /v1/watchers, /v1/heartbeat) — the LAPI's own API activity, dominated by agent/bouncer polling. Metric: rate(cs_lapi_route_requests_total[$__rate_interval]) by route (labels route, method) on the lapi pod.
panels.title: LAPI Requests/s (by route)

panels.description: LIVE. LAPI request latency p95 and p50, computed from the request-duration histogram. Metric: histogram_quantile(q, sum by (le)(rate(cs_lapi_request_duration_seconds_bucket{pod=~"crowdsec-lapi.*"}[$__rate_interval]))). Rising p95 = the LAPI is under pressure.
panels.title: LAPI Request Latency (p95 / p50)
Parser sources — lines read/sec
panels.description: Line-rate per acquisition source, summed across every agent. These metrics come from a 5-pod agent DaemonSet, so each agent only sees ITS OWN node's logs. Every query here sums ACROSS agents (no pod/instance in the by-clause) to give a cluster-wide view — which is precisely what the crowdsec-web-ui cannot do, since it scrapes crowdsec-agent-service and that ClusterIP load-balances to one arbitrary agent per poll. The `source` label is the container log path, so each series is one watched workload.

panels.title: Parse success vs failure rate
panels.description: Unparsed is NOT automatically a fault: an acquisition tails a container's whole stdout, and only lines matching that app's parser count as ok. Traefik for example emits WRN/ERR application lines alongside access-log JSON, so a high ko rate there is normal. Judge a source as broken only if ok stays at zero for days while the app is genuinely being hit.

panels.title: Scenario buckets — overflows/sec (bans fire here)
panels.description: An overflow is a scenario firing — the moment a decision is created. Aggregated across agents. NOTE scenarios listed in simulation.yaml still overflow and still appear here; they simply do not ban. That is the intended state for everything added in the wave 1+2 rollout.

panels.title: Scenario buckets — events poured/sec
panels.description: Events entering each scenario's bucket. Compare against overflows: a high pour rate with no overflow means the scenario is seeing traffic but not reaching its threshold — healthy. Pours at zero means the scenario never matches anything, i.e. dead coverage worth investigating.

panels.title: AppSec — requests/sec by engine
panels.description: AppSec (WAF) request volume. NOTE cs_appsec_block_total does NOT exist in this deployment — only reqs and rule hits are exposed — so blocked-vs-allowed cannot be charted. Use the rule-hits panel as the proxy for enforcement activity.

panels.title: AppSec — rule hits
panels.description: AppSec rules matching. This is the closest available signal to 'requests the WAF acted on', given cs_appsec_block_total is not exposed.

panels.title: Parser timing — avg seconds per line
panels.description: Average parse time per line, derived from CrowdSec's parsing histogram (sum/count). Rising time on one source usually means an expensive grok or a log format that regressed. Aggregated across agents.

panels.title: Node hits by parser stage
panels.description: Which individual parser nodes are matching, top 15. This is the panel that tells you whether a newly-added collection is doing anything at all: a parser with zero node hits over days is installed but dead — the exact failure mode that got LePresidente/gitea removed after Forgejo turned out to emit a different log format.

list.label: Scenario
